For all the grandstanding about the debt limit, they always raise it. If only people could recognize political theater when they see it.

One point that's missing from this video is that the president has veto power over the budget that congress approves. In fact, Bill Clinton used this veto power during his presidency, which led to the shutdown of the government for a very short while. So the president too authorizes the budget.
I didn't know POTUS was able to veto a bill, thanks for the info.

Congress can also break up the Budget into multiple bills to continue funding essential services and individual portions of the government. That way Congress can avoid so much party budgetary wrangling between the miriad of departments fighting over taxpayer money. Republicans tried to do this during the last debt ceiling "crisis" but this is where the Executive branch has leverage. The executive branch can threaten to veto and shutdown government and lay the blame on Congress inability to pass a monolithic budget that doesn't include the President's budgetary demands and pet projects.

Its a political game of who can make who look bad to win popularity, to the detriment of taxpayers and government employees. All of this, with a short-sighted view of fiscal wisdom.

I do support the ability of the US government to enter into debt. BUT, it should be under extraordinary circumstances of war and disaster, not a matter of course.

If the US continues to incur more and more debt, the faith in the dollar will be lost THAT way much, and in a much, much more explosive and painful manner. Cutting spending is literally the only option to fix the sinking ship, and even that has to be dramatic. Sorry, I'm just a resident of one of the colonies here (Canada). Can anyone ELI5 TV licence fees, please?

The bbc is a public broadcaster and to own a television that plays live TV you have to have a license. It's £145ish a year per household. It pays for all the bbc TV channels the iPlayer (like netflix but only bbc stuff) all the radio stations including the world service. This way the BBC stays ad free, and independent of owners. If you don't have a license you can't watch live TV as it's broadcast in your own home or else you can get fined or even sent to prison (for a tiny amount of time). Most people are happy to pay and like the bbc. There is a vocal minority that think the BBC is a waste of money and should be privatized. These people are generally right wing and consider BBC to have a left wing bias.
